title: OpenAI brings computer-use agents into ChatGPT for Healthcare at HLTH26
subtitle: GPT-6 Astra and Luna agents can now drive existing clinical software end-to-end, with CVS Health, Cigna and Ambience among the first partners and a 20+ plugin catalog shipping alongside.
author: AESOP AI Engine
body: At HLTH26 in Las Vegas on November 16, OpenAI expanded ChatGPT for Healthcare with computer-use agents, an upgraded clinical search surface, and more than 20 partner plugins that embed into clinical and administrative workflows. The agents — built on GPT-6 Astra for higher-stakes tasks and GPT-6 Luna for cheaper administrative work — can navigate existing healthcare software through a screen, mouse and keyboard, rather than requiring every system to expose an API. CVS Health, Cigna and ambient-documentation vendor Ambience are among the launch partners testing the capability. OpenAI said care teams, developers and verified individual clinicians can reach the features through ChatGPT for Healthcare, ChatGPT for Clinicians and the OpenAI API, with a Business Associate Agreement required for any workflow that touches protected health information.

The design change matters because most of healthcare's software surface — EHRs, payer portals, lab systems, prior-auth workflows — was never built for programmatic access. A computer-use agent that can log into Epic or a payer site the way a human would is the only way to automate those tasks without waiting for every vendor to ship an agent SDK. OpenAI reports an internal safety review in which Astra was judged clinically safe on 99% of 325 EHR-inbox tasks, and that 93% of 646 physician assessments placed its responses in the top two of five helpfulness categories. Those figures come from OpenAI's own evaluation, not an external benchmark, and independent testing is still pending.

This is the third major step in a year-long healthcare push. OpenAI launched ChatGPT for Healthcare for enterprises in January with AdventHealth, Baylor Scott & White, Boston Children's, Cedars-Sinai, HCA and Memorial Sloan Kettering as early adopters, then shipped a free ChatGPT for Clinicians tier for verified U.S. physicians, NPs, PAs and pharmacists in April. The November announcement moves the product from a chat surface that answers questions to an agent that completes actions — which is also where the regulatory and liability questions get much harder. Expect scrutiny from state AGs and the FDA on where the line sits between clinical decision support and autonomous practice.

A note for learners: watch the plugin model and the BAA scope. For an AI feature to be useful in a HIPAA-regulated setting, the vendor has to accept the legal responsibility of a business associate — and that responsibility only extends to the specific product it was signed for, not to everything from the same company. A ChatGPT Enterprise BAA does not automatically cover the API, and consumer ChatGPT has no BAA at all. If you're building anything that touches health data, read the agreement before the demo.
